title: perf(objectql)!: a cascade delete removes a relation's children as one predicate delete per chunk
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9UbbGfxE9QQTsFJp457cGiCViY)_

Part of #33699

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — the published hook dispatch shape for cascaded children changes (`dispatch.mode` 'record' → 'per-row', `options.multi`, before-hooks run before the set delete); BREAKING banner + ADR-0087 disposition in the changeset; one CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER review owed before the queue
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no `skills/**` file teaches a cascaded child's `dispatch.mode`, `referentialCascadeDelete` or a sibling-count hook (`git grep` of `dispatch.mode`, `referentialCascadeDelete` and `per-row` over `skills/`: the only hits teach predicate writes in general and stay true); the spec's own hook docs are updated here

**No longer waiting on #33928 (as of `5ed247661`):** it landed on main as #34033 and is in this tree by the merge at `321a8668f`. Ruling 6893661036 precondition (1), the #33782 parity pins merged as #33927, is met: all 8 cases green at `5ed247661`, in `Test Core (8/8)` and locally. CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER record 6908865874 on `5ed247661`: PASS.

**c1 stays open on #33699.** Ruling 6893104201's c1 (the walk's collect probe, re-probe and recycle-bin snapshot read the same child rows) is not done here, so this PR does not close the card.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:删除一条记录时,级联删除的子记录不再逐条删除,而是每 500 条一批、一条 `DELETE … WHERE id IN (…)` 删掉;每个子记录的删除前后钩子、实时事件、回收站、权限拒绝回滚都保留。
- **为什么改**:删除一个带 10 条明细的商机,今天要 155 条 SQL,随明细数线性增长;本 PR 实测降到 58 条(SQLite 与 PostgreSQL 相同,其中 1 条是按调用者读权限核对本批子记录),中位耗时约减半。
- **风险与回滚**:级联子记录的钩子上下文从 `dispatch.mode: 'record'` 变为 `'per-row'`(带 `options.multi`),同批子记录共用一个 `dispatch.scope`,前后两个阶段各拿一个新的 ctx,所以挂在 ctx 上的临时值到不了删除后钩子(改放 `ctx.dispatch.scope`,按 `ctx.input.id` 分键);同批删除前钩子全部先跑、再统一删除。调用者无权删除或无权读取的子记录、以及级联途中由钩子新写入的子记录,都退回今天的逐条删除。回滚 = revert 本 PR。
- **先看**:`packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-planning.ts`(`deleteCascadedChildren`:只批量已收集的成员,其余与被收窄的批次逐条删除)、`packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts`(谓词删除分支里的范围核对与逐行实时事件)、changeset 的 FROM → TO 段。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run src/engine-cascade-delete-batch.test.ts`,预期 15 个用例全绿(`Tests 15 passed (15)`)。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## What changes

Ruling 6893661036 (option F1), replacing point 4 of ruling 6893104201; points 1–3 stand.

- **The walk** (`engine-cascade-planning.ts`): for a `cascade` relation the walk now collects the relation's dependents across the whole root set and hands them to `deleteCascadedChildren`, which issues ONE predicate delete per chunk of 500 (`REFERENCE_PROBE_BATCH`, under `MAX_BULK_PER_ROW_HOOK_ROWS` = 10,000) through the public `delete()`: `where: { id: { $in: chunk } }`, `multi: true`. The chunk therefore runs every child's `beforeDelete` (per-row, ADR-0058 Addendum II), one `deleteMany`, then every child's `afterDelete`. A child's own children are walked by the predicate arm's existing `cascadeDeleteRelations` (#27004), joining the root's set, so grandchildren are batched too.
- **The marker** (`engine-top-level.ts`, `engine-middleware-and-context.ts`, surface amendment 6893212568): the cascade-issued token gains an optional id set, and `claimReferentialCascadeDelete` matches a predicate delete whose `where` is exactly `{ id: { $in } }` naming that set. Every per-row context, both phases, carries `referentialCascadeDelete: true`.
- **Security parity, point 2** (`engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts`): a claimed cascade batch always reads its doomed rows through the middleware-composed AST. If a requested child is missing (a scope that narrows a predicate delete where it refuses the by-id one), the engine throws an engine-internal `CascadeBatchNarrowed` before any hook or write; the walk catches only that and deletes the chunk by id, so the caller meets today's refusal and envelope and the cascade rolls back. A driver with no `deleteMany` (or a floored external driver) keeps the by-id path. One cascade can show both shapes.
- **Realtime, point 1**: a cascade batch publishes one `data.record.deleted` per child from its pre-image, never the bulk `data.records.deleted`.
- **Point 3**: no new refusal; the bulk per-row hook ceiling is asserted only when the child has delete-side hooks, and a chunk never exceeds 500.
- **Spec prose**: the `HookContext.dispatch.mode` and `referentialCascadeDelete` TSDoc now say a cascaded child is `'per-row'` with `multi`, and that the token can name an id set. No `.describe()` and no schema shape changed (`check:docs` green, nothing regenerated).
- **SQL shape emitted** (SQLite driver log, `DEBUG=knex:query`, warm delete): inside the transaction, one doomed read `select * from bench_line_item where id in (?, x10)`, then one `delete from bench_line_item where id in (?, x10)`; the sharing cleanup now runs once per chunk (`select/delete from sys_record_share … record_id in (?, x10)`, same for `sys_share_link`); the audit pair stays per child.
- **A dependent the collected set never held** (`engine-cascade-planning.ts`, record 6899834361 S2): only `cascadeSet.members` are batched; a row a hook of the same cascade wrote after the set was collected is deleted by id, as the root of its own cascade, with its own recycle-bin entry, as before the batch.

## What a hook on a cascaded child sees (FROM → TO, as in the changeset)

- FROM `ctx.dispatch.mode: 'record'` and `ctx.input.options` `{ where: { id } }` TO `ctx.dispatch.mode: 'per-row'`, with `ctx.dispatch.index` its position in the chunk and `ctx.input.options` carrying `where: { id: { $in: [...] } }` and `multi: true`. `ctx.input.id` and `ctx.previous` still name the child's own row, and `ctx.referentialCascadeDelete` is still `true` on every per-row context, in both phases, grandchildren included.
- FROM `ctx.result` in a cascaded child's `afterDelete` being the driver's by-id answer TO `ctx.result` absent, as on every per-row delete context. Read `ctx.previous` for the deleted row.
- FROM `ctx.dispatch.scope` one scratch object per cascaded child TO one object shared by every child of the chunk, in both phases (the scratch of one caller write, which the chunk now is).
- FROM one context object for a cascaded child's `beforeDelete` and `afterDelete` TO a fresh context per row per phase, so a value a `beforeDelete` handler leaves on `ctx` no longer reaches that child's `afterDelete`. Keep cross-phase state in `ctx.dispatch.scope`, keyed by `ctx.input.id`.
- The one behaviour that flips: the chunk runs every child's `beforeDelete`, then the one set delete, then every child's `afterDelete`. Before, each child ran before → delete → after in turn. So a `beforeDelete` hook that counts a child's remaining siblings now sees them ALL present, where it used to see one fewer at each step. Judge the whole batch instead: on `ctx.input.options.multi === true` read the target set from `ctx.input.options.where` (the shipped last-administrator guard does exactly this, and reaches the same verdict as before), or use `ctx.referentialCascadeDelete === true` to tell the cascade from a hand delete.
- A chunk the caller's scope narrows falls back to today's by-id deletes for that chunk, so the caller still meets the same refusal and the whole cascade rolls back: a child the caller may not delete, which a predicate delete would skip, and a child the caller may not read, which the by-id delete refuses through its re-read of the row (the cascade asks the caller's read door for each chunk's ids before batching it). Such a chunk keeps today's shape, `'record'` with no `multi`, so one cascade can show both shapes. A driver with no `deleteMany`, a floored external driver, and a cascade into the organization object (deleted by id or not at all) keep the by-id path too, and so does a child the walk finds that the cascade's collected set never held (a row a hook of the same cascade wrote after the set was collected): it is deleted as the root of its own cascade, with its own recycle-bin entry, as before.

## Tests

- `packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-delete-batch.test.ts` (15 cases, a driver that rolls back for real and logs its writes): before x N, one `deleteMany`, after x N with the write count observed from inside each hook; `dispatch.mode: 'per-row'`, `index` 0..N-1, `options.multi`, `previous` = own row, the marker on every per-row context; **`dispatch.scope` is one object across the chunk's six dispatches, a value left on `ctx` in `beforeDelete` does not reach `afterDelete`, and the same value kept in `dispatch.scope` keyed by `input.id` does, with the by-id shape as control (three scopes, the ctx stash arrives)**; the sibling-count flip (`[3, 3, 3]`); grandchildren batched and marked; 501 children = two set deletes (500 + 1); realtime per-row; rollback on a before-phase and an after-phase refusal; the narrowed-chunk fallback (today's 403 envelope, nothing deleted, only `'record'` dispatches ran); an allowed fallback keeping today's shape beside a batched relation; no `deleteMany` keeps by-id; the read-door fallbacks (hidden and refused, hidden and allowed, all readable as control); a cascade into the organization object deleted by id.
- `packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/capture.test.ts`, new top-level `describe`: **a `cascade` dependent a hook of the same cascade writes after the set was collected is deleted by id with a recycle-bin entry of its own (`note/n9`), while the collected members stay rows of the root entry (`account/acc1`, `contact/c1`, `contact/c2`, `note/n1`)**.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/cascade-delete-security-parity.test.ts` (#33927, on main, not edited here): 8 of 8 green on this head.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/cascade-batch-read-scope.test.ts`: a child hidden by a select-class policy and admitted by a delete-class policy refuses the parent's delete on both legs; control deletes on both.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.test.ts`, top-level `describe` `[F1]`: the shipped last-administrator guard reaches the same verdict on the batch and on the by-id path, refused and allowed.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-summary-rollback.test.ts`: one expectation re-triaged (see Acceptance notes).

## Acceptance notes

- The one fixture re-triaged: on a runtime that cannot roll back, a refusal raised after a chunk's set delete (a failed roll-up recompute) now finds the whole chunk deleted, where the per-child walk had deleted only the children before the refusal. The changeset says so.
- Not done here, from ruling 6893104201's c1: the walk's collect probe, re-probe and the recycle-bin snapshot still read the same child rows. Behaviour-neutral, left on the card.
- The spec's `dispatch.mode` TSDoc lists the by-id fallbacks and does not name the dependent the collected set never held (S2 of record 6899834361): left as is so this round moves no `packages/spec` text; the changeset names it.
- Surface, named explicitly: `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.test.ts` and `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/cascade-batch-read-scope.test.ts` (test-only, outside the claim's objectql file surface, both ordered by a ruling or a prior record). `packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/capture.test.ts` is inside it.

## Verification

Head `5ed247661`: `origin/main` at `31eb2aeda` merged (`321a8668f`, 128 commits, no textual conflict; `hook.zod.ts` auto-merged), then `74ef4e4bc` (S2) and `5ed247661` (S1). The net diff against `origin/main` is the same changed lines as before the merge (diffed: identical `+`/`-` line sets over the same 10 files), plus this round's three files. Interplay read: #34033 now judges a `multi: true` write by the bulk write scope unless the engine runs it by id, so the batch's `{ where: { id: { $in } }, multi: true }` is no longer refused as a by-id write of `[object Object]`; a row the sharing write scope narrows out is answered by `CascadeBatchNarrowed` and goes by id, as before. #33782 is closed; its pins are the #33927 file above.

<details><summary>Which shape each parity case took (one-off probe, not committed)</summary>

A temporary object-less `beforeDelete` recorder was added to the parity file through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` and removed (restored blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty); 8 of 8 green with it. The four cases that land run batched: `f_all` (12 lines, 2 notes), `m1`, `m2`, `h1`, every child `per-row multi=true marker=true`. The four refused cases fall back: `r1`, `f_u` (unreadable child, the read door misses it) and `r2`, `f_e` (edit-shared child, readable, so the batch's write-scope read misses it and `CascadeBatchNarrowed` crosses the real security and sharing chain back to the walk); each shows `_a` as `record`, then the refusal at `_b`'s by-id delete. So every refusal in the file comes from today's by-id door, and none from the batch.

</details>

## Update at `616735ceb` (review 6896079092)

Fix round for the CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER review 6896079092 (VERDICT: FAIL) and review 6896089195, by session `session_01QsR2jUg7BKfRBcTPyMxbLh` (the earlier body above is kept as written). Commits: `4029ca241` (M1, S1, N1 to N4), `bb5e34b5d` (the read-seam guard and the walk's host type, the two CI reds of `4029ca241`), `eab93bab0` and `7d2730a95` (merges of main; the second brought in the #33927 parity pins), `616735ceb` (changeset count).

| finding | disposition | evidence |
|:--|:--|:--|
| M1 · the batch drops the read scope the by-id child delete enforces | **fixed** | The reviewer's reading holds, measured: the new pin is red on the batch leg at `89dff98f6` (objectql source of that head, `{ kind: 'landed' }`, the hidden child deleted) and green on the by-id leg (403). Fix: before a chunk is batched, the walk asks the caller's read door (`find(child, { where: { id: { $in: chunk } }, fields: ['id'] })` under the walk's context) and deletes the chunk by id when any id is missing, so the by-id path gives today's answer. A read the door refuses (declared 4xx) also routes to by-id; a store fault propagates. |
| S1 · a cascade into `sys_organization` newly refused 409 | **fixed** | `childName !== ORGANIZATION_OBJECT` in `batchable`; pinned in objectql. No other refusal of the same one-term shape found (list in Acceptance notes of this update). |
| N1 · `dispatch.mode` fallbacks | fixed | TSDoc names all four by-id cases (narrowed or unreadable chunk, no `deleteMany`, floored external driver, the organization object) and says the before-hooks run before the set delete per chunk of 500 within one relation. |
| N2 · stale "ctx.input identical" | fixed | `referentialCascadeDelete` "Why a declared key" now says `ctx.user`/`ctx.session` are identical and `ctx.input`/`ctx.dispatch` tell nothing apart either. |
| N3 · changeset FROM to TO omits `ctx.result` | fixed | New FROM to TO bullet: `ctx.result` in a cascaded child's `afterDelete`, the driver's by-id answer, is now absent; read `ctx.previous`. The `dispatch.mode` value is stated as the code sets it, `'per-row'`. |
| N4 · "the caller's scope" | fixed | The comment in `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` says the doomed read is the caller's WRITE scope and that the read scope is proven by the walk. |
